parsed_output.analysis: The specification requires a parallel/orthogonal composition with three independently activatable collision-avoidance regions, activation of the whole sub-machine only on a possible frontend, rear-end or pedestrian collision detection, and concurrent activation of the different controls. The PlantUML model defines CollisionAvoidanceSystem as a normal composite state containing three nested composite states Frontend Collision Avoidance, Rear-End Collision Avoidance and Pedestrian Collision Avoidance. Entry to CollisionAvoidanceSystem is unconditional and the whole system is terminated on Collision Avoided. The three children are modelled as exclusive nested sub-machines with a generic Collision Detected trigger and they are not declared as orthogonal/parallel regions.

issues.reason: Specification requires three orthogonal regions of the active mode that allow concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls. The model nests three sub-states inside CollisionAvoidanceSystem without a parallel/orthogonal composition, so in standard UML/PlantUML they are interpreted as an exclusive choice, not concurrent regions.
issues.where: state CollisionAvoidanceSystem { state "Frontend Collision Avoidance" ... state "Rear-End Collision Avoidance" ... state "Pedestrian Collision Avoidance" ... }

issues.issue: Sub-machine entry is unconditional instead of detection-triggered
issues.reason: Specification says the sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected. The model enters CollisionAvoidanceSystem from [*] with no trigger/guard, so activation is unconditional.

issues.issue: Whole system exit on Collision Avoided
issues.reason: Specification does not define a global deactivation on Collision Avoided and implies per-region activation/deactivation on detection. The model terminates the entire CollisionAvoidanceSystem on Collision Avoided, preventing independent concurrent operation of the three controls.

issues.issue: Generic detection trigger used for all three regions
issues.reason: Specification implies activation per type of collision: frontend, rear-end or pedestrian. The model uses the same generic 'Collision Detected' event for all three regions instead of distinct Frontend Collision Detected / Rear-End Collision Detected / Pedestrian Collision Detected triggers.
issues.where: Idle --> Braking : Collision Detected in Frontend, RearEnd and Pedestrian states

issues.issue: Regions are forced to start together rather than activate independently
issues.reason: Specification allows concurrent activation of different collision avoidance controls on their respective detections. The model starts all three sub-machines together when CollisionAvoidanceSystem is entered, with each sub-machine beginning in Idle, so independent per-detection activation is not modelled.

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
